name: label_ranges
value: {'low single digit': (1, 3), 'low to mid single digit': (2, 5), 'high single digit': (7, 9), 'low teens': (11, 13), 'mid to high teens': (15, 19), 'high teens': (17, 19), 'low 20s': (20, 23), 'low-to-mid 20s': (20, 26), 'mid-20s': (24, 26)}
reason: Vendors give words, not numbers. The total-dram notes read 'mid-20s' as about 24-26% and 'low 20s' as about 20-23% (Micron call notes); the other words use the same three-point split of a decade.

name: approx_halfwidth_pp
reason: A '~X%' value is read as X +/- 1 pp.

name: base_2025_log_sd
reason: Mirae's 2025 production (293.1 bn Gb) is an estimate made in Dec 2025. KGI (37.6 EB) and Yole (38 EB) put 2025 demand within 1-1.5% of Mirae's demand; 3% also covers the gap between production and demand definitions.

name: mirae_server_lp_split
reason: No source says whether Mirae counts Grace/Vera LPDDR in 'server' or in 'mobile'. TrendForce counts it in mobile; Yole in data center. We draw the fraction f that sits in Mirae's server line from U(0,1) and remove it from that line only, so the bits are never counted twice.

name: server_lp_2023
reason: No 2023 figure; LS Securities gives 1.1 bn Gb for 2024, so 2023 was small. Set to 0.

name: mobile_includes_tablets
reason: Mirae's 'mobile' line implies about 1.4 bn devices at 11.2 GB, more than phones alone, so it holds tablets too. Tablets get the phone unit and content growth; no tablet content figure exists.

name: content_freeze_floor_pct
reason: Phone, PC and 2027 mobile content growth: the low end is a full freeze (0%). TrendForce, IDC and Micron report spec cuts and frozen configurations in 2026, but no source gives a number for the floor.

name: mobile_content_2027_pct
reason: No source gives 2027 GB per phone. The LPDDR notes recommend flat to +5% from the 2026 value; we use a triangle 0 / 2.5 / 5%.

name: other_2026_log_sd
reason: Mirae 'other' (20.3 bn Gb) has no second source on the same basis. 10% covers a consumer-unit swing of the size seen elsewhere in 2026 (AIB cards -10%, JPR).

name: auto_from_mirae_other
reason: Auto DRAM (2-3% of bits) is taken out of Mirae's 'other' line. The brief puts auto in LPDDR; no source gives the LPDDR share of auto DRAM.

name: gddr_2027_growth_pct
reason: No GDDR bit forecast exists. Gaming card units fall (JPR -10% in 2026, -5.9% CAGR) while GB per AI card rises (RTX PRO 6000 96 GB). We take a flat centre, +/-10%.

name: other_2027_growth_pct
reason: Max is Mirae's +4.9% for 'other'. Min -10% matches the consumer-unit fall seen in 2026 (JPR AIB). Mode flat. No direct source.

name: hbm_share_annual_average
value: h(year) = (h(end of prior year) + h(end of year)) / 2
reason: TrendForce gives HBM wafer shares at year ends (18/22/30%); the bit model needs annual averages. 2026 uses AMAT (Mar 2026, 15%) as the low end and Samsung (Oct 2026, ~20%) as the mode.

name: new_fab_half_year
reason: TrendForce (Jul 2026): new fabs ramp from 2H27; Micron: ID1 and Tongluo output from mid-2027. A fab that starts mid-year adds about half its year-end capacity to the annual average, so the mode of each new-fab addition is half of Mirae's 2027 step.

name: cxmt_hbm_linear_ramp
reason: CXMT HBM wafers are given at year ends (SemiAnalysis: 5, 30, 55 kwpm). The annual average is the midpoint of the start and end values.

name: priority_allocation_2027
value: HBM -> server LPDDR -> server ECC -> ALR for the rest
reason: LTAs, prepayments and supplier statements put HBM and server first. Server ECC grows at its own supply guide (TrendForce RDIMM +15-20%, Mirae +22.7% as max) and is not renormalised; phone, PC, GDDR, other and auto share what is left. Auto keeps its share of total bits.

name: trade_ratio_rise_2027
reason: Micron (Sep 2026) says the trade ratio rises with HBM4/HBM4E, so rho >= 0. Goldman (Jun 2026) gives 3-4x against Micron's 3x: the top of that range is +33%, the midpoint +17%. r(2025) = r(2026): no source gives a 2025-2026 change.

name: hbm_node_gain_equals_standard
reason: HBM core dies use the same DRAM nodes (1b, 1c), so HBM bits per wafer grow at the same node-migration rate n as standard DRAM. No source splits the two.

name: node_gain_ceiling
reason: The upper end of the 2027 node gain is one full node step for the whole fleet in one year, which no year has reached.

name: rubin_ultra_units_2027_m
reason: UNSUPPORTED. No source gives 2027 Rubin Ultra package units. Rubin's own launch year (2026) was 1.5-2.4 M chips (KeyBanc, Morgan Stanley; hbm-gddr notes). Rubin Ultra ships from 2H27, so we take about half that, widened to 0.5-1.5 M. Used only to move HBM demand, not supply.

name: server_ddr5_share
reason: TrendForce puts DDR5 at ~90% of server bits in 1Q25. DDR4 server parts reached end of life at Samsung (Dec 2025), SK hynix (Apr 2026) and Micron (1Q26), so the share only rises. No 2026 number exists.

name: pc_ddr5_share
reason: UNSUPPORTED beyond 'DDR5 passed 50% of PC DRAM in 2H24' (TrendForce). No later figure exists in text form (Apacer's chart is an image).

name: combination_weights
reason: Equal weights for time series, supply model and guidance. The supply model has no track record, so we cannot estimate its error variance; with few data points equal weights usually beat estimated ones (the 'forecast combination puzzle'). We report the inverse-variance result as a check.

name: ts_min_train_years
reason: Rolling-origin backtest starts after 10 years of data.

name: quarterly_vendor_path
reason: Only Samsung and SK hynix give 2026 quarterly QoQ bit guidance. The industry path uses their bit-weighted QoQ; 1Q26 is solved so the four quarters sum to the annual total.
